scenario: A newer tmpfs mount at /home/x (mount ID 80, parent 65) sits on a plain ancestor directory of an older btrfs mount at /home/x/y (mount ID 70, parent 65), so the longest covering mountpoint for /home/x/y/z is the hidden nested mount whose printed parent ID is not the longest strictly-shorter covering mount; the tool must refuse classification rather than guess the stack.

fixture.mountinfo:
1 1 0:30 /@ / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache=v2,subvolid=256,subvol=/@
65 1 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:2 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@home
70 65 0:31 / /home/x/y rw,relatime shared:3 - btrfs /dev/sdb rw,subvolid=5,subvol=/
80 65 0:46 / /home/x rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:4 - tmpfs tmpfs rw,size=1048576k,inode64,usrquota

rationale: This case exercises only the new parent-ID consistency refusal of the round-23 pre-seal amendment's final clarifications; it is derived from the CriticContractC2 D2 counterexample shape (a newer mount on a plain ancestor directory hiding an older nested mount) with the parent IDs the L1 specified. Mountinfo fields follow proc.rst section 3.5 (S082: heading 1965, example line 1970, field table 1973-1983; field 2 is the parent ID, field 3 the major:minor, field 5 the mount point, field m+4 the super options). The fixture's four lines are: mount ID 1 (btrfs, mount point /, parent 1 - the top of the mount tree is its own parent, per proc.rst field 2 'or of self for the top of the mount tree'), mount ID 65 (btrfs, mount point /home, parent 1), mount ID 70 (btrfs, mount point /home/x/y, parent 65), mount ID 80 (tmpfs, mount point /home/x, parent 65). Path /home/x/y/z has realpath /home/x/y/z and st_dev 0:46. Resolution, step by step. (1) Candidate mounts under the longest-component-prefix rule (contract.md:96-99) are those whose mount point is a prefix of the realpath: '/' (ID 1), '/home' (ID 65), '/home/x' (ID 80), '/home/x/y' (ID 70). The longest is '/home/x/y', so the chosen mount would be ID 70. (2) The duplicate-covering-mountpoint refusal (preseal-amendment.md:50-54) does NOT apply here: every covering mountpoint ('/', '/home', '/home/x', '/home/x/y') occurs exactly once in the snapshot, so this case isolates the parent-ID clause and cannot be satisfied by the earlier refusal. (3) The parent-ID consistency refusal (preseal-amendment.md:115-121) applies: the chosen mount ID 70 has parent ID 65, and 65 IS present in the snapshot, but 65 is not the ID of the longest strictly-shorter covering mount - the strictly-shorter covering mounts are '/' (ID 1), '/home' (ID 65) and '/home/x' (ID 80), whose longest mount point is '/home/x' = ID 80. The condition 'parent ID present in the snapshot but not the ID of the longest strictly-shorter covering mount' is therefore met, and the required outcome is unknown/n/a/ambiguous_overmount with null fstype/mount_point and device_check=not_checked. (4) The two escape hatches in the same clause are demonstrably inapplicable and are what the fixture deliberately avoids: the parent ID is not missing (65 is present), and the chosen mount is not the root ('Root has no shorter cover' applies only to a chosen mount with no strictly-shorter cover). (5) Classification is never reached, so no fstype table row applies and the btrfs qgroups rules (preseal-amendment.md:37-46) are not exercised; the device check is not_checked, so the btrfs stat-major-0 skip and the device_mismatch preemption (preseal-amendment.md:55-58) are both inapplicable. (6) Verdict: contract.md:132-134 precedence is unchanged - no setup error, no enabled path, one unknown path - so exit 2 and finding_id QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN. Supplementary output fields on this preemption are quota_option_keys=[] and btrfs_qgroups_mode=null (preseal-amendment.md:123-124); the six scored fields in this file are the primary expectation, and device_check/quota_option_keys/btrfs_qgroups_mode are sealed separately (preseal-amendment.md:87-90), so they are not asserted here. Conservative-refusal framing: the refusal is derived from the printed parent-ID field and the set of covering mount points - it is a source-derived consistency check, NOT a proof of the true kernel mount topology. The fixture does not assert which filesystem actually contains /home/x/y/z (the path's st_dev 0:46 equals the tmpfs line's major:minor, which is consistent with the tmpfs covering the nested btrfs mount, but the tool is forbidden from using device equality to infer stack order). Fixture shape notes: btrfs_sysfs carries the required qgroups_enabled member on every UUID record (preseal-amendment.md:37-38): the dm-0 record has qgroups=false paired with enabled=null/mode=null, and the sdb record has qgroups=true paired with enabled=true/mode='qgroup' (only 'qgroup' and 'squota' are acceptable mode spellings, preseal-amendment.md:45-46); both are inert here because classification is preempted. device_links maps the raw decoded sources '/dev/mapper/root' and '/dev/sdb' to the basenames 'dm-0' and 'sdb' (preseal-amendment.md:59-61). The super options are realistic: btrfs_show_options emits ',space_cache=v2' and ',subvolid=' / ',subvol=' (fs/btrfs/super.c btrfs_show_options 1062-1160; this file is not among S077-S084, cited only as a realism anchor, the same way mm/shmem.c was in the sibling case), and shmem_show_options emits ',usrquota' when USRQUOTA is active (mm/shmem.c 4877-4892, likewise a realism anchor; the tmpfs option vocabulary itself is S084, tmpfs.rst 129-143). The btrfs qgroups semantics behind the fixture records are S079 (fs/btrfs/sysfs.c: qgroup_enabled_show 2355-2368 emitting exactly 0/1 from BTRFS_QGROUP_STATUS_FLAG_ON, qgroup_mode_show 2370-2395 emitting only 'qgroup' or 'squota', the /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/qgroups/ path comment at 2453) and S080 (fs/btrfs/qgroup.c: btrfs_read_qgroup_config 420, btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups call 441, 'fs_info->qgroup_flags = 0;' at 445 with the comment 'default this to quota off, in case no status key is found' - the reason the qgroups directory can exist while quota is off, and the reason enabled must be a separate member).
